ratings.reason: Uploading existing footage is a clear ingestion path into video reconstruction, and reauthoring source footage is consequential. The quote does not explain the resulting interaction or reconstruction controls, so mechanism and impact remain somewhat under-evidenced.

This is an unusually clean early instance: an existing preliminary design is uploaded, encoded into latent state, and used to generate design inspiration. Conditioning generation on a user's draft transfers readily beyond UI design and was less settled in 2022.

NoRe directly transforms a user-produced journal artifact into a different medium. Journal-to-music generation is a distinctive use of source conditioning for personal reflection, although the evidence does not establish outcome improvements.

Conditioning exclusively on a user's accumulated highlights is a strong personal-corpus design move with ownership and reflection implications. The quote does not say what Quologue generates or how highlights enter that process, limiting mechanism clarity and evidential confidence.

The system clearly ingests an existing multimodal diary—text, photos, and metadata—and generates a context-matched VR environment. Using heterogeneous personal records to reconstruct immersive memories is both legible and notably more ambitious than routine image transformation.

Uploading a primer melody and querying models from it is a clear source-conditioned composition workflow. It is useful and transferable to other media, but continuation from a seed artifact is a comparatively settled generative interaction.

Turning an existing lo-fi user flow into privacy-review outputs reframes source conditioning as design critique rather than content restyling. That move addresses a real UX breakdown and transfers broadly, though the quoted 'three-tiered outputs' are not described well enough to reconstruct.

The input-image-to-synthetic-image relationship is explicit and central. The metaphor-driven research-through-design framing makes the familiar image-conditioning mechanism conceptually interesting, but the available evidence does not show a strong practical outcome shift.

Transforming personally made textile collages into memory videos is an inventive bridge from physical craft to generation. However, the collages appear to have been created immediately for this activity, making the fit weaker than cases involving genuinely pre-existing artifacts.

The letter clearly conditions story generation through extracted events and emotions, but the evidence does not establish that it pre-existed the request rather than being authored as the request specification. The emotional-reframing claim is also not evaluable from this quote.

TubeLens is a standout exemplar: it converts a user's accumulated behavioral history into a generative self-portrait specifically to support critical reflection on algorithmic profiling. The move is explicit, consequential, non-obvious, and readily transferable to other platforms and personal-data traces.

A designer's existing clothing-image collection supplies the learned style condition for new sketches, making the owned artifact central rather than incidental. It is a strong instance of personal corpus conditioning, although the broader design pattern is not domain-independent without adaptation.

Collaposer transforms an existing photo collection into reusable storytelling assets, with text serving as an additional organizing condition. The source material is essential and the workflow solves a concrete preparation burden, though it is an evolution of familiar asset-extraction pipelines.

Generating a product description from its photo is a valid and broadly transferable source-conditioned interaction. It is also close to the default multimodal-LLM use case, and the quote only describes a displayed study stimulus rather than a rich authoring mechanism.

Video-to-decomposed-multitrack generation is a clear and unusually productive cross-modal conditioning move that gives sound designers editable material rather than a monolithic result. Its object-centric sound workflow is compelling but more domain-specific than the strongest exemplars.

Original physical-space footage visibly conditions video-to-video generation alongside text, fitting the pattern. Mixed-reality spatial editing may make the workflow consequential, but the truncated introductory quote neither specifies the full interaction nor demonstrates its outcomes.

DataSway explicitly parses an existing visualization in SVG and raster forms and uses it as conditioning state for element-wise animation generation. The representation-aware decomposition is reconstructable and more interesting than generic image animation, though it remains specialized to visualization authoring.

PicMe centrally converts a user's face photo into a stylized vector portrait, so pattern fit is unambiguous. The transformation is useful but technically and interactionally conventional, with limited transfer beyond personalized visual-product workflows.

DiaryPlay turns an author's existing prose story into structured, refinable interactive-vignette elements. The extract-and-scaffold mechanism is clear and consequential, although it is uncertain whether the story is truly pre-existing or composed specifically for this authoring workflow.

Accumulated personal reflections becoming a persistent RAG source is a strong form of conditioning on prior user-produced material. The pattern generalizes well to other longitudinal personal corpora, but the quote does not show what is generated or how retrieval shapes the visible interaction.

Users select existing objects from web content or physical-camera imagery and convert their 2D appearances into 3D objects. This is a legible and useful cross-dimensional transformation, though live capture sits near the pattern's pre-existing-artifact boundary and the XR setting limits transfer.

The final image is explicitly conditioned on an original image, style model, and prompt. Its speculative camera framing is interesting, but the source may be captured as part of the generative request rather than already possessed, and the quote offers little interaction detail.

LumiMood conditions changes on the user's current 3D scene and generates a coordinated lighting and post-processing treatment. This is a clean artifact-aware authoring aid, but stylizing an existing scene is a fairly expected design move and remains tied to 3D workflows.

CareerCraft explicitly ingests user documents and reflections, extracts their content with an LLM, and generates structured experience cards. The document-to-structured-profile move is clear, consequential, and broadly reusable, although free-text reflections may partly be authored for the interaction itself.

Generating digital-twin responses from participant data plausibly fits source conditioning and is conceptually interesting. However, 'participant data' is unspecified: the quote provides no ingestion path, artifact type, visible interaction, or assurance that the material is user-owned and pre-existing.

A single existing image conditions six generated views, with text providing an additional constraint and scores supporting assessment. The mechanism is exceptionally clear, but image-conditioned novel-view generation is increasingly standard and only one component of the broader orchestration system.

The user's existing code cell is automatically captured as source material for documentation assistance, a consequential reduction in specification effort that transfers broadly across programming tools. The quote only shows transmission to the server; generation and resulting UI must be inferred from the title.

RoomDreaming clearly ingests an existing room image and derives depth, elements, and spatial structure to condition design generation. Preserving source-space constraints addresses a genuine weakness of prompt-only interior generation and provides a legible mechanism transferable to other spatial-design tasks.

The photo-to-cartoon transformation is mechanically explicit, but it appears to be an ancillary personalization step within a larger career-imagination system rather than the paper's central design contribution. A predefined image-edit prompt is also a very settled source-conditioning pattern.

The cited passage is only a general claim that current technology makes generation from dream records possible. It does not show that the authors' interface ingests a user's record, routes it into a generator, or produces the described environment.
ratings.disqualify_reason: The evidence quote does not support the pattern assignment for the paper's own interface; it describes a technological possibility rather than an implemented source-conditioned interaction.
